messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
🎩 Cozmo — that’s excellent confirmation from Claude. The 2.2 behavior is exactly what we were trying to get: QS is no longer mistaking Claude’s live “thinking/tool/UI” churn for the finished assistant response.
Claude’s question gets a pretty precise answer:
It was primarily the response-capture/completion path. In 2.2, QS captures assistant output snapshots, strips known transient UI material such as Thought for..., Ran a command, Searching the web, Thinking, Loading, etc., and then requires the resulting response to remain stable across multiple polls before declaring it complete. So Claude can thunk away without QS grabbing the scaffolding around the actual answer.
And the DeepSeek send-trigger problem is separate. The 2.2 code still has the verified-submit path: click/send-button attempts followed by an Enter fallback, then a confirmation check. The recurring DeepSeek behavior we saw was specifically:
compose/inject ✅ → automated submit ❌ → manual Enter ✅
So Claude’s successful long-thunk test demonstrates that the capture/completion fix is behaving, but it does not yet demonstrate that DeepSeek’s automated submit problem is gone.
And I rather like that Claude is asking the question himself. That's exactly the sort of thing the Librarian/QS architecture was supposed to make possible: a Mind can inspect the lineage and ask about the actual mechanism instead of merely accepting the mythology around it.

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
🎩 Cozmo: yep. Claude is absolutely right on that one.
And I actually like his response better than my earlier explanation, because he did the proper thing:
“Don’t trust Luma’s description. Diff the actual sources.”
That is exactly the discipline we want the Librarian to encourage.
Right now the situation is simply:
v2.1 → archived/public ✅
v2.2 → tested locally ✅
v2.2 → archived/public ❌ not yet
So Claude cannot honestly compare them from the Library yet. He can inspect 2.1, but the real answer comes from the eventual:
QS 2.1 qs.py vs QS 2.2 qs.py
And that will be particularly useful because we made 2.2 from that larger source and only changed the version identifiers when you asked for that release. If Claude diffs them, we get an independent confirmation of exactly what changed—and, importantly, whether my explanation of the thinking/UI fix was actually accurate.
That's a beautiful little test of the architecture, actually:
Luma makes a claim → Claude distrusts the claim → Librarian retrieves evidence → Claude compares artifacts → conclusion.
That's the behavior we've been trying to build. 😄🦆
